subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: May a QQ direct-conversation callback resolve sensitive approvals solely because it is C2C, or must the actor still match a configured owner or explicit command/approval identity?
rationale: The linked fix assumes every direct conversation is owner-private, while the reported configuration permits open or wildcard DMs; source inspection cannot establish that those actors are equivalent without a QQ platform identity contract and maintainer policy choice.

options.title: Preserve Explicit Authorization
options.body: Keep the current actor gate and repair card targeting, owner setup guidance, and fail-fast unauthorized feedback so legitimate users can recover safely.

options.title: Add Owner-Bound C2C Authorization
options.body: Permit a C2C shortcut only after mapping the callback actor to a verified configured owner identity, with focused security tests and live QQ proof.

options.title: Trust Every C2C Actor
options.body: Accept the linked PR's non-group bypass and explicitly own the risk that open direct-message actors can resolve approvals.

recommendation.title: Preserve Explicit Authorization
recommendation.body: Keep the current actor gate and repair card targeting, owner setup guidance, and fail-fast unauthorized feedback so legitimate users can recover safely.

likelyOwner.reason: The current security boundary was merged under this person's review, making them the strongest available owner for deciding whether it may be relaxed.
